fundamental.thesis: Zydus Lifesciences is a large Indian pharma company that earns from US generics, India branded formulations and consumer products, and it is now adding medtech and US specialty businesses through acquisitions (Amplitude Surgical, Comfort Click, Assertio). In Q1 FY27 revenue grew +21.9% YoY to ₹8,017 cr, but much of that growth came from acquisitions. PAT fell -35.9% to ₹940 cr, EBITDA fell -9.3%, PAT margin compressed from about 18.6% (FY26) to 11.7%, and EBITDA margin dropped from 31.2% to 25.4%. Exceptional charges were only ₹18 cr, so the profit drop comes from the business itself and not from one-off items. US revenue was already shrinking (-5.7% in Q4 FY26), which means the earlier gRevlimid-type windfall is fading. On the desk's yardstick for pharma (P/E plus EV/EBITDA), the stock looks cheap on trailing numbers: P/E of 21.7x is below the 28-40x sector range and in the cheapest 8% of peers, and EV/EBITDA of 16.1x is about 25% below the peer median. However, forward P/E of 23.3x sits only 9% below the peer median, at P38, and is higher than trailing P/E, so earnings are expected to fall. With the stock at 90% of its 52-week range, I grade valuation as fair rather than cheap. The biggest risk is that Q2 results on 4 Nov confirm continued margin erosion from loss-making medtech (-28.9% segment margin) and falling US sales, at a time when the US Commerce review of tariffs on generics still hangs over the stock.

Varun Beverages is a large franchise beverage bottler with 54 plants across India and 9 overseas franchise markets, and its growth is now being partly bought through acquisitions such as Twizza in South Africa and the Kenya business. In the September 2026 quarter, revenue growth accelerated to +33.2% (Rs 6,608 cr) from +19.4% in H1, but EBITDA margin fell 140 bps to 21.6%, gross margin fell 334 bps to 53.1%, and PAT, which I derived from cumulative figures at about Rs 798 cr, rose only about 8-11% for a margin of about 12%. On P/E, cross-checked with EV/EBITDA, the stock looks fair rather than cheap: trailing P/E of 56x sits within the 40-65x FMCG norm and near the 51.5x peer median (P67), EV/EBITDA of 34.6x is at the peer median, and a position near 90% of its 52-week range leaves limited upside. The biggest risk is that a premium multiple is being paid while packaging costs and acquisition-related depreciation and finance costs (up 34.5% and 53.5% in the quarter) squeeze margins, and consensus upside offers little comfort because the stated +36% conflicts with a price of about Rs 527 implied by the 52-week position and market cap, against which the Rs 538 mean target is only about 2% higher.

Torrent Pharmaceuticals is a branded-formulations company led by its India chronic-therapy business, with further sales in Brazil, the US and Germany, and it expanded its India franchise by merging JB Pharma in 2026. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 50.8% YoY to Rs 4,979 cr, compared with +55.0% in Q1, but that headline growth is mostly the JB deal: the base business grew about 18% and base India grew 20% against 12% for the market, while PAT growth slipped from +3.0% to -9.6% (Rs 534 cr) and PAT margin fell from 17.9% to 10.7% a year ago despite a steady 33.5% EBITDA margin and solid cash generation (H1 operating cash flow of Rs 2,452 cr is about 2.2x H1 PAT; the 4.59x shown compares H1 cash flow with Q2 PAT alone). Using P/E and EV/EBITDA against peers, the stock is expensive: trailing P/E of 69.1x is above the 28-40x sector benchmark and 36.4x peer median (P92), EV/EBITDA of 37.5x compares with a 21.4x median (P85), and the Rs 1.5L cr market cap may omit the 4.19 crore merger shares, so these multiples could be understated. The biggest risk is that this premium needs JB integration to lift profits, yet FY EPS estimates have been cut 5.0% in 30 days and 7.0% in 90 days while JB's international business fell 7% and Germany fell 7%.

fundamental.thesis: IDFC First Bank is a mid-sized private bank with a retail-heavy loan book and a strong deposit franchise (CASA 48.4%), now scaling fast after years of rebuilding profitability. In Q2FY27, PAT was ₹1,045 cr, up 196.5% YoY off a depressed base and above ₹1,000 cr for a second straight quarter. Loans grew 30.1% YoY (22.2% excluding FCNR(B)-backed loans, up from 20.6% in Q1), deposits grew 25.9%, and asset quality kept improving: net NPA fell from 0.48% to 0.44% to 0.40%, and gross NPA was 1.32% vs 1.61% at FY26-end. Valuation is graded on P/B plus ROE, as the sector card requires for lenders, not on trailing P/E: P/B is 1.31x (P36 among peers, 11% below the 1.5x median) against annualised ROE of only 10.6%, which is below the 12% bar for 'cheap', so the stock is fair. The 38x trailing P/E is distorted by weak FY26 earnings (PAT ₹1,611 cr), and the 11x forward P/E sits exactly at the peer median. The main risk is that rapid growth is outpacing the bank's profitability engine: CASA slipped from 50.8% to 48.4% and NIM was diluted by FCNR(B) funding, Q2 ROA fell to 0.93% from 1.06%, and capital adequacy (CAR) dropped to 15.05% from 15.6% while the loan book grows about 30%.

GAIL is India's largest gas transmission and marketing company, with pipelines giving it a steady tariff business (58% margin in H1) and marketing as the larger, more cyclical profit source (Rs 7,131 cr of H1 segment profit vs Rs 3,964 cr from transmission). Subtracting Q1 from H1 gives Q2 FY27 revenue of about Rs 47,301 cr, up about 33% YoY (from +16.7% in Q1), and PAT of about Rs 4,724 cr, up about 138% (from +96%), but PAT margin slipped from 11.3% to about 10.0% and EBITDA margin from 18.3% to about 15.7%; these are derived figures, the press release shows a lower Rs 45,924 cr revenue and Rs 4,650 cr PAT (basis unconfirmed), and the pre-computed trajectory signals are unreliable because they compare H1 with Q1. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick, I grade valuation fair: the 11.56x is at the peer median and the 14.65x trailing P/E is just above the 8-14x Energy range, but both look stale because 14.65x implies trailing profit of about Rs 7,500 cr, less than H1 PAT alone, while annualising H1 gives about 6x, which is flattering if profits are near a peak. The main risk is durability: analysts raised this year's EPS by about 30% in 30 days but next year's by only 0.6%, suggesting they see a one-year spike, and the marketing profits behind it could fade while the Petronet force majeure has cut GAIL's RLNG allocation to zero.

fundamental.thesis: Indian Bank is a mid-sized public-sector bank with a ₹8.74L cr deposit base and ₹7.11L cr of advances, and about two-thirds of its loans go to retail, agriculture and MSME borrowers (RAM 65%). In H1FY27 total income grew 16.1% YoY to ₹44,333 cr and PAT grew 28.1% to ₹6,897 cr, but Q2 includes a one-off NSE listing gain of ₹1,387 cr. Stripping it out, underlying PAT growth looks closer to high single digits, and the core trend is mixed. Gross NPA improved from 2.23% to 1.86% to 1.61% with PCR at 98%. Against that, NIM slipped from 3.37% to 3.24%, credit cost rose from 0.21% to 0.47% to 0.71% over three quarters, and deposits are growing slower than loans (12.5% vs 17.5% YoY). fundamental.thesis: Deepak Fertilisers is a mid-cap ammonia-chain business. It makes industrial chemicals (nitric acid, IPA, methanol), it is a leading Indian producer of technical ammonium nitrate (TAN) for mining, and it sells crop nutrition (NPK, specialty fertilisers), with large new capacity at Gopalpur (TAN) and Dahej (nitric acid) due to start in Q2 FY27. On the official filings, FY26 revenue grew 12.0% to ₹11,506 cr, but PAT fell 21.8% to ₹739 cr. Profitability has been shrinking through the year: PAT margin slid from 8.1% (H1) to 7.0% (9M) to 6.4% (full year), and EBITDA margin from 17.3% to 14.6%. The filing-extracted trend table has no Q1 FY27 revenue or PAT, and the unverified yfinance figure (PAT ₹490 cr on ₹1,886 cr revenue) looks like it may include a one-off. Treating this as a cyclical chemicals business, we judge it on EV/EBITDA: 11.1× is about half the broad-market median (bottom 15% of the market), but it is above the 5–8× the sector card calls normal for chemical cyclicals at mid-cycle. Trailing P/E of 16.9× sits inside the 12–22× Materials range, so overall we grade it fair. The forward P/E of 10.6× and analysts raising this year's earnings estimates by 43% over 30 days already assume the new plants succeed. The biggest risks are a slow ramp-up at the new plants with debt high (debt/equity about 0.76) and free cash flow negative (−₹396 cr in H1 FY26), together with raw-material squeeze from the Middle East and a falling-margin trend.

Dalmia Bharat is a mid-sized Indian cement maker with 54.7 MTPA installed capacity across 12 states, expanding toward 67 MTPA, including the acquired Jaypee assets in Central India. Q2FY27 revenue, derived as H1 minus Q1 because the Q2 row is blank, was about ₹3,563 cr (+4.3% YoY, slowing from +10.7% in Q2FY26), and PAT was about ₹-201 cr after ₹339 cr of exceptional items; volume rose only 3%, EBITDA per tonne fell from ₹1,013 to ₹746, below the ₹900-1,100 healthy range, and management expects more fuel and Central India cost pressure in Q3. On the capital-intensive yardsticks of EV/EBITDA and EBITDA per tonne, I grade valuation fair: 12.3x EV/EBITDA is on depressed earnings, the 35.0x trailing P/E (Materials benchmark 12-22x) is distorted by one-offs, and the P19 EV/EBITDA and P15 P/B ranks are less useful because they compare against the broad market, not cement peers; the 15.7% position in the 52-week range offers some support, but this is not clearly cheap with FY EPS estimates cut about 19% in 30 days. The biggest risk is that fuel inflation and Central India dilution keep margins falling while capex of ₹3,200-3,400 cr continues, leading to further estimate cuts.

fundamental.thesis: PCBL Chemical is India's largest carbon black manufacturer and one of the world's top-3 by installed capacity (900,000 MTPA post Mundra commissioning in Q1FY27), serving tire OEMs, industrial users, and a growing specialty segment alongside Aquapharm oil-field chemicals — a structurally improving but still cyclical business. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive cyclical (per Sector Card), 17.72× sits below the broad-market peer median of 23.3× (P33 rank) and the forward P/E of 21.22× is at the upper end of the Materials benchmark range (12–22×), making valuation fair — the 50.77× trailing P/E is severely distorted by Q3FY26's near-zero PAT quarter and must be discounted; structural tailwinds from India–US tariff reduction, India–EU FTA, and Russian supply contraction are real multi-year catalysts but are already partially priced. Using EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for chemical cyclicals, the stock looks expensive at 18.1x, or very roughly 15x on my estimate using trailing EBITDA of about Rs 730 cr before net debt, against a 5-8x mid-cycle norm; trailing P/E of 34.6x and forward P/E of 22.3x also sit above or at the top of the 12-22x Materials range, and the fair reading against peers carries little weight because it uses a broad-market comparison, not chemical peers. Q2FY27 revenue rose 73.6% YoY to about Rs 2,896 cr, easing slightly from +78.1% in Q1 (the table's 'accelerating' label and the Rs 167 cr and Rs 315 cr FY26 revenue figures look like data errors, as the filing shows Rs 1,668 cr for Q2FY26), while PAT growth improved from +5.4% to +16.7% (Rs 301 cr), PAT margin recovered from 7.7% in Q1 but remains well below 15.7% a year ago, and operating margin fell 501 bps to 19.48%, so the jump in sales has not produced matching profit, and the data does not show how much of it is organic. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-intensive business, 25.4x is only 9% above the broad-market median of 23.3x (P57) and trailing P/E is 46.9x, so the grade is fair, but this is a weak comparison because no hospital peer set is available, and a forward P/E of 26.6x already assumes a large earnings rise while FY EPS estimates have been cut 4.3% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that margins fail to recover while debt/equity sits at 1.21x, although interest cover of 4.29x and H1 cash conversion of 1.91x CFO/PAT (FCF Rs 594 cr) provide some cushion for now.

It is now funding a heavily loss-making quick home-help business called InstaHelp. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹537 cr, up 41% YoY, faster than FY26's +36%. fundamental.thesis: C.E. Info Systems (MapMyIndia) is India's dominant digital mapping and location intelligence platform, holding a near-monopoly in B2B GIS/API/SaaS services with 83.5% of revenue from high-margin subscription-type map data; it competes with no listed domestic peer of comparable depth, giving it structural pricing power. Q1FY27 headline revenue grew +14.9% YoY to ₹139.72 cr (PAT ₹50 cr, +7.9% YoY, margin recovering to 35.6% from a 9MFY26 trough of 22.8%), but the acceleration is almost entirely device-driven (GPS/IoT +204% YoY to ₹23.11 cr) — the core mapping segment, which is the durable cash engine, grew only 2.28% YoY, a saturation signal that the headline masks. On valuation, trailing P/E of 36.88x sits above the IT sector median upper bound of 30x and EV/EBITDA of 29.08x is at P64 vs broad peers (+24.7% premium to median), but forward P/E of 22.49x (P48, a 39% discount to trailing) and the stock sitting at just 10.9% of its 52-week range (near ₹795 low vs ₹1,998 high) together grade this 'fair' rather than 'expensive' — the price has corrected more than fundamentals warrant, but the core-segment stall prevents a 'cheap' call. The biggest risk is that device revenue is lumpy, lower-margin, and non-recurring — if it fades, headline growth reverts to 2-3% core growth — and the September 2026 NSE volume-movement clarification request alongside a subsidiary director resignation introduces near-term governance uncertainty at a time when sell-side EPS estimates are being cut (90d Δ: −4.6% current FY, −6.5% next FY).

The last quarter extracted from the official filings, Q1 FY27, shows revenue up 12.2% YoY to ₹1,776 cr and PAT up 68.5% to ₹469 cr. That jump follows a weak FY26 (revenue +1.9%, PAT -44.6%) and is distorted by a one-time ₹108 cr net tax benefit and a ₹194 cr coal-mine surrender provision. The Q2 FY27 results filed on 19 Oct are not yet in the trend table, and the unverified yfinance figures (PAT ₹33 cr) hint at a sharp seasonal or underlying drop, so the 'accelerating' trajectory label should not be trusted. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-heavy business, 11.4x (P16 vs the broad market) and P/B of 1.23x look reasonable, but trailing P/E of 22.9x is above the 10–18x utilities band, so overall it is fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is roughly ₹2,000 cr of disputed claims (UPPCL ₹473 cr, AP sand-mining notices ₹857 cr, ICICI recompense ₹570 cr, a ~₹124 cr JAL guarantee), about 18% of market cap and none provided for, made worse by the CFO and Company Secretary both leaving on 30 Sep 2026.

CESC is a West Bengal-regulated power utility with a coal mine and other power operations, and its earnings depend heavily on tariff orders and regulatory income. Valuation is fair on EV/EBITDA of 10.92x, supported by a trailing P/E of 14.68x inside the 10-18x utilities range and P/B of 1.81x for 12.5% ROE; I gave little weight to the cheap broad-market peer rank because it does not compare utilities, and I ignored the 348% dividend yield, the +59.7% target upside (which does not fit the roughly Rs 170 price implied by the market cap and EPS) and the -100% estimate revisions as likely data errors. fundamental.thesis: Nava Limited is a diversified India-Zambia conglomerate spanning thermal and solar power (India merchant + MEL Zambia), ferro alloys (SiMn, ferro silicon), coal mining, and nascent avocado agriculture — a complex earnings mix where Zambian energy and Indian merchant power together drive the majority of consolidated EBITDA, making it a power-cycle hybrid rather than a regulated annuity. Using EV/EBITDA as the correct yardstick for this capital-intensive power and materials business, NAVA trades at 10.0× vs a broad-market median of 23.3× (P10 percentile, -57% discount) — unambiguously cheap on an absolute and relative basis, though the extreme reported Debt/Equity of 20.68 inflates EV and partially explains the valuation discount. The central risk to the cheap-valuation thesis is that extreme leverage combined with USD 67.9 mn of Zambian ZESCO receivables and MEL Phase 2 commissioning slippage to mid-2028 could constrain equity value or trigger dilutive financing if power prices or INR/USD conditions deteriorate.

fundamental.thesis: NHPC is India's largest hydropower generator. It earns a regulated return on equity on power plants once they are commissioned, so earnings growth depends on new capacity starting up, not on power prices. The latest quarter in the trend table showed revenue up 18.5% YoY to ₹3,808 cr but PAT up only 4.2% to ₹1,178 cr (30.9% margin). FY26 revenue grew 11.9% to ₹11,615 cr and PAT 25.2% to ₹3,766 cr, but EBITDA margin has fallen from about 66% (FY25) to about 54% (FY26), and finance costs take about 16% of revenue. Because this is a capital-intensive regulated business, I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA and P/B+ROE. On those measures the signals conflict: EV/EBITDA of 25.5x is rich for a utility, and a P/B of 1.85x for a ROE of only 9% is not cheap. On the other side, the forward P/E of 11.9x (bottom 14% of the market) and P/B in the bottom 16% suggest the market already expects the Subansiri Lower and Parbati-II earnings ramp, so overall I grade it fair. The biggest risk is weak cash conversion: free cash flow was -₹3,850 cr in FY26, CFO/PAT was 0.62x, and leverage is high (debt/equity about 1.13x). Earnings also depend on about ₹939 cr of provisional revenue that CERC has not yet approved, and Q2 results are due on 4 Nov 2026.

fundamental.thesis: NLC India (NLCINDIA) is a Navratna PSU lignite miner and thermal power generator (~0.51 GW installed capacity) with a nascent renewable pipeline, operating under regulated and quasi-regulated tariff structures. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue accelerated to +23.3% YoY (₹4,717 cr vs ₹3,826 cr in Q1FY26), driven by a 25% YoY jump in power generation to 8,262 MU — a genuine volume pickup — but Q1FY27 PAT is not yet extracted from official PDFs, and a structural concern is visible: PBT grew only 9.76% vs revenue's 23.29%, and EBITDA margins have contracted from a FY25 peak of 42.6% to 36.0% in Q1FY27 as interest and depreciation from aggressive capex outpace operating gains; tariff realisation has also fallen sharply from ₹3.74/kWh (FY25) to ₹2.45/kWh (FY26), squeezing per-unit economics even as volumes rise. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive regulated utility (per sector card), the 9.88× multiple sits at the P10 peer percentile — a 58% discount to the broad-market median of 23.3× — and trailing P/E of 12.75× is at the low end of the 10–18× Utilities benchmark, making valuation clearly cheap; forward P/E of 11.99× marginally below trailing signals consensus expects modest earnings growth, though the single analyst covering this stock (target ₹390, +54%) provides very weak signal. The dominant risk to the thesis is further tariff compression from CERC regulatory resets combined with rising debt servicing on a capex-heavy balance sheet (D/E flagged as elevated by yfinance; FCF was ₹-2,779 cr in FY26), which could keep PAT margins structurally below FY25 levels even as revenue grows.

Intellect Design Arena is a mid-cap financial-services software vendor built around its eMACH.ai platform, with about 500 customers across 62 countries. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13.0% YoY to ₹855 cr, slowing from +36.2% in Q2 FY26 and +20.6% in Q1 FY27, while PAT rose only 1.8% to ₹104 cr; PAT margin improved from 11.7% to 12.2% QoQ but remains below 13.5% a year ago, and platform revenue slipped from ₹141 cr to ₹133 cr QoQ with license-linked revenue flat at ₹457 cr. Valuation is fair on trailing P/E plus growth delivery, the IT yardstick used here: 31.15× is just above the 22-30× sector range but inflated by the weak ₹28 cr Q3 FY26 quarter, while the 18.43× forward P/E assumes a roughly 70% EPS rebound that looks demanding as FY EPS estimates have fallen 9.8% in 90 days; the peer ranks are broad-market rather than IT-specific, and the 53% dividend yield, 4.96 debt/equity flag and +76.5% target upside look like feed errors and were not used (the 52-week position and market cap imply a price near ₹757, or about +25% to the ₹947 target). The biggest risk is that over ₹100 cr of AI investment and slowing platform growth keep margins under pressure before the deal pipeline, including 21 new eMACH.ai customers and 8 Destiny Deals, turns into revenue, while the impact of the cyber security incident disclosed on 2026-10-28 is not yet known from the data provided.

fundamental.thesis: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles is India's second-largest OEM and houses the Jaguar Land Rover luxury brand globally; post the CV demerger (effective Oct 2025) it is a pure-play on domestic EVs and JLR's BEV transition, with domestic EV mix rising to ~14.3% of volumes. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive OEM, TMPV trades at 7.09× vs the sector median of 18.3× (P0 — cheapest in peer group), and forward P/E of 7.15× vs peer median 20.8× — deeply cheap, but that discount reflects real distress: negative TTM ROE of -1.1%, extreme leverage (D/E 65.31), and 90-day EPS estimate cuts of -20.6%. The core risk is that JLR's four planned BEV launches fail to fill the Jaguar volume gap while high leverage leaves no cushion for further margin disappointment.

Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for this capital-intensive business, the stock at 21.0x sits 38% below the 34.0x sector median (P24), and its 31.25x trailing P/E is inside the 28-45x benchmark, but I grade it fair rather than cheap because the peer set is dominated by richly priced capital-goods names with different business models and the stock is at 95.6% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is that growth is partly acquired and funded by new shares and debt, with H1 capex of Rs 10,522 cr leaving only about Rs 2,805 cr of free cash flow and logistics margin falling to 8.59% from 13.98%.

fundamental.thesis: Eicher Motors is India's dominant mid-weight motorcycle manufacturer through Royal Enfield (87% domestic market share in the segment) with an expanding global footprint and a 50:50 JV in VECV (commercial vehicles), giving it a structurally premium and defensible franchise. Q1FY27 revenue surged 31.6% YoY to ₹6,632 cr with PAT up 21.4% to ₹1,463 cr — however, PAT margin compressed 181 bps YoY to 22.0%, and the PAT growth meaningfully lagging revenue growth signals cost absorption headwinds despite strong volumes; the EBITDA margin trend is more encouraging, expanding to 31.0% in Q1FY27 from ~24–25% in mid-FY26, suggesting operating leverage is materialising at the gross level even as below-the-line costs (finance, depreciation from capex ramp) create PAT drag. On the sector-preferred P/E yardstick, trailing P/E of 37.9× sits at the P80 peer percentile and commands a 40% premium to the sector median of 27.1×; EV/EBITDA at 33.7× is P100 in its peer set and 84% above the sector median — on both measures the stock is expensive relative to peers, and the forward P/E of 28.8× (still P83) reflects already-priced-in earnings growth, leaving limited re-rating room. The key risk is the combination of a RISK_OFF macro (FII selling, rising crude costs for consumers, Auto sector underweight tilt) with a stock already in the top quartile of peer valuations and PAT margins visibly compressing — any festive season demand disappointment or further input cost spike would catalyse a derating without a valuation cushion.

JSW Steel is a large Indian steelmaker that sold a record 7.46 MT in Q2FY27 (+13% YoY), with auto-sector sales up 36%. Revenue growth accelerated from +9.8% in Q1 to +20.6% (₹54,486 cr), and PAT rose 225.6% to ₹5,359 cr, though the YoY figures use a low, restructured base; PAT margin was flat at about 9.8-9.9%, the 'contracting' signal is distorted by FY26's ₹18,051 cr one-off gain, and EBITDA per tonne fell about 11% QoQ from ₹14,990 to ₹13,329 despite rising 24% YoY. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a steel cyclical, the stock is expensive: the reported 12.6x, or roughly 9x on my estimate using annualised Q2 EBITDA and net debt, is above the 5-8x mid-cycle norm, and the 13.8x trailing P/E and 'cheap vs peers' verdict carry little weight because of the one-off gain and a peer set that includes paint and adhesive companies. The biggest risk is that steel spreads narrow from here, with the stock at 92% of its 52-week range and EBITDA per tonne already falling sequentially, leaving little room for error.

fundamental.thesis: Exide Industries is India's dominant lead-acid battery manufacturer serving automotive OEM, replacement, and industrial segments, and is executing a transformative ₹4,900+ cr bet on lithium-ion through its wholly-owned EESL gigafactory subsidiary (6 GWh Phase-1 capacity, all four production lines now fully equipped and operational). Revenue growth has sharply accelerated from -2.1% (Q2FY26) to +17.7% YoY in Q1FY27 (₹5,528 cr), with PAT growing +27.9% to ₹351 cr — driven by 25%+ auto OEM growth for three consecutive quarters, double-digit 2W/4W replacement demand, and a 20%+ export recovery; however, PAT margin contracted slightly to 6.3% from 6.9% in Q4FY26 as sulfur costs surged +393% YoY and INR depreciation added to import-linked input pressure. Trailing P/E of 40× sits well above the Auto sector benchmark of 18–28×, grading as expensive; EV/EBITDA of 18.6× (P40 among peers, fair) and forward P/E of 23.9× (within sector range) indicate near-term earnings recovery is already priced in, and the stock sitting at 80% of its 52-week range leaves asymmetrically limited upside — made worse by a consolidated Debt/Equity of 11.31× flagged in the snapshot that contradicts the standalone 'zero debt' claim and warrants verification against EESL's project borrowings. The key risk is the ₹4,900+ cr (rising to ~₹6,300 cr post-FY27) equity commitment to EESL — if the Li-ion gigafactory ramp lags, faces BOM-cost headwinds from Chinese incumbent competition, or generates lower-than-expected pack economics, ROE (already depressed to 6.2% TTM from the capex drag) will remain structurally low and compress the premium valuation.

Revenue growth slowed from +12.0% in Q4 FY26 to +6.5% in Q2 FY27 (Rs 1,691 cr), while PAT fell 28.6% to Rs 121 cr, EBITDA margin dropped from 20.6% to 17.8%, and PAT margin fell from 9.5% to 7.1%; H1 FY27 PAT fell 30.4% and converted to cash poorly (CFO/PAT 0.50x, FCF about Rs 6 cr), although implied Q1-to-Q2 margins improved, guidance was maintained and Q2 deal wins were USD 213 mn. The biggest risk is that margins and cash conversion stay weak as auto-client spending and AI-led pricing pressure persist, making the low price a falling knife rather than a value entry.

Q1FY27 consolidated revenue grew +14.4% YoY to ₹4,255 crore (reversing four consecutive quarters of -1% to -2.5% decline), but PAT fell -81% YoY to ₹60 crore and EBITDA contracted -14.5% to ₹555 crore, as the Industrial Essentials segment swung from +₹131 crore profit to -₹70 crore loss — revenue growth is not flowing to earnings; PAT margin stands at just 1.4% vs 4.3% in the comparable prior period. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick per the sector card for this capital-intensive commodity name, at 14.5× vs sector peer median 17.9× (P40 rank), the stock screens modestly below peer median, but the sector card's own 5–8× mid-cycle commodity benchmark and a negative TTM ROE of -7.7% mean the current multiple implies significant recovery — graded fair, with limited margin of safety on a structurally depressed EBITDA base. The central risk is that China's elevated soda ash inventories (~1.8 million tonnes), sustained price-dumping into Asian markets, and structurally uncompetitive US operations (already requiring ₹1,837 crore goodwill impairment in FY26) keep Industrial Essentials loss-making well beyond Q1FY27, with EPS estimates cut -21.8% over 90 days and a pending NSE exchange clarification (2026-09-29) and auditor change in UK subsidiaries (2026-09-26) adding governance uncertainty.

fundamental.thesis: India Cements is a mid-sized South India cement maker with 14.75 MT of capacity (Q1FY26). It is now controlled by UltraTech, so the story depends on a turnaround under new ownership rather than on stand-alone strength. The latest extracted figures are stale: they run only to 9MFY26 (filed Jan-2026), and the Q2FY27 results filed on 2026-10-17 have not been indexed yet. In those older numbers, cumulative revenue growth picked up from -0.2% YoY in Q1FY26 to +4.8% in H1FY26 and +10.9% in 9MFY26 (₹3,256 cr). The company was still losing money, though the loss margin narrowed from -13.0% to -3.9% (9M PAT ₹-127 cr), while EBITDA margin slipped from 9.4% (H1) to 7.5% (9M), so the fall in costs per rupee of sales has not held. Because cement is capital-intensive, I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA. At 25.9× it sits well above normal cement multiples and above the broad-market median of 23.3×, and the 116× trailing P/E reflects barely positive earnings. The 1.06× P/B and the price near its 52-week low look cheap only on the surface. The 20.6× forward P/E already assumes a turnaround, while analysts have cut this year's EPS estimates by about 21% in the last 30 days. Grade: expensive. The biggest risk is that EBITDA per tonne keeps lagging the healthy ₹900–1,100 band. Rising crude-linked fuel and freight costs and a risk-off market make that more likely, and the turnaround that today's price assumes would then be pushed back.

Q2FY27 revenue rose 38.0% YoY to Rs 1,427 cr (Q1: +43.1%), but this growth is flattered by the RMIL acquisition, with no organic split provided, while PAT growth slowed from +14.3% to +6.0% (Rs 102 cr), PAT margin fell from 9.1% in H1FY26 to 7.2% in H1FY27, and operating cash flow was negative at Rs -68 cr in H1 despite Rs 208 cr of PAT. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick, 24.0x is in line with the broad-market median of 23.3x (P52), and trailing P/E of 33.2x is near the 35.2x median (P47), so the grade is fair; there are no close peers, and the multiple is well above the 5-8x the sector card gives for mid-cycle chemical and steel cyclicals, a comparison of limited use for a recycler. Key feed figures look unreliable: the 64% dividend yield is implausible against a Rs 7.70 dividend, the 29.93 debt/equity is probably a percentage (about 0.30x), and the +35% target upside conflicts with market cap and 52-week data implying a price near Rs 1,700 (about +11-13%), so the biggest risk is that growth keeps failing to reach profit and cash while FY-EPS estimates are being cut by 1.8% and next-FY by 3.0% despite 10 of 10 buy ratings.

fundamental.thesis: Jindal Stainless (JSL) is India's #1 stainless steel producer and #5 globally ex-China, operating 4.2 MTPA capacity across 120+ product grades on a ~₹44,000 cr TTM revenue base, with strong structural demand from government infrastructure programmes (railways, highways, airports). Q1FY27 revenue grew +10.5% YoY to ₹11,279 cr (stable, not accelerating from FY26's +9.3%), but PAT margin has contracted from 7.4% in FY26 to 6.8% in Q1FY27 as raw material costs at ~70% of revenue compress the spread; PAT growth has decelerated sharply from +27.4% in FY26 to +7.7% YoY in Q1FY27. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick (the correct metric for capital-intensive steel, per sector card), JSL trades at 6.59× — inside the 5–8× mid-cycle cyclical range and at the 4th percentile vs 473 broad-market peers — grading CHEAP, corroborated by forward P/E (13.68×) sitting at a discount to trailing P/E (18.27×), pricing in continued earnings growth. The biggest risk to this thesis is raw material cost volatility (nickel, ferro-alloys at ~70% of revenue) combined with structural Chinese overcapacity, which could further erode the already-contracting EBITDA margin (13.1% Q1FY27 vs 13.7% peak in FY26).

SAIL is a large government-owned integrated steel maker, with Bhilai, Bokaro and Rourkela contributing about 81% of revenue, and it benefits from India's protected steel upcycle. H1 FY27 revenue rose 10.7% YoY to Rs 58,243 cr, improving from about +8% in H1 FY26, while EBITDA margin edged up from 10.9% to 11.5%; PAT jumped about 192% to Rs 3,395 cr, but EBITDA rose only about 14% (roughly Rs 840 cr against a PAT gain above Rs 2,200 cr), so the jump is not explained by operations, and the missing Q1 FY27 row means Q2 momentum cannot be isolated. On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for capital-intensive steel, the 8.84x snapshot is slightly above the 5-8x mid-cycle norm, while the 22.3x trailing P/E looks stale because filing-based trailing PAT of about Rs 5,516 cr implies about 13.6x, so I grade it fair: P/B of 1.3x with about 10.9% annualised ROE is not a clear bargain, the broad-market peer ranks are a weak comparison, and rising estimates (FY EPS +18.5% over 30 days) are offset by little upside, since the Rs 185 mean target is only about 2% above the roughly Rs 182 price implied by the 52-week position, not the stated 13.2%. The biggest risk is that the PAT surge proves non-recurring or steel spreads narrow, and no spread or EBITDA-per-tonne data was available to test this, with Rs 23,457 cr of provisionally priced government sales and a 0.79 current ratio adding balance-sheet risk.

fundamental.thesis: ITC is a diversified Indian conglomerate where the cigarettes franchise (~70% of operating profit) funds FMCG Others (branded packaged goods), Agri Business, Paper & Packaging, and Hotels — it is priced on a structural conglomerate discount rather than as a pure FMCG compounder, and the sector card explicitly names it 'its own animal.' Q1FY27 revenue of ₹29,523 cr shows a misleading +27.6% YoY surge driven almost entirely by excise duty reclassification post GST-compensation-cess expiry (Feb 2026), where cigarette excise surged 538% to ₹10,409 cr; the underlying picture is PAT down -15.6% YoY to ₹4,509 cr (including an exceptional ₹406 cr Sproutlife gain) with EBITDA margin compressed sharply from 32.7% to 20.0% — this follows a weak multi-year trajectory of FY26 PAT +1.0%, FY25 PAT -0.8%, and CFO/PAT deteriorating to 0.59× in H1FY26 (below the 0.6 warning threshold), signalling earnings stagnation and weakening cash conversion. On P/E, ITC at 16.93× sits at P0 (cheapest in sector) vs a peer median of 51.5× and the 40–65× FMCG benchmark, and is equally at the floor on EV/EBITDA (12.1× vs peer median 34.6×) and P/B — the valuation case is unambiguous on any yardstick, but the discount is structural (tobacco overhang, conglomerate penalty, no near-term demerger catalyst) and a re-rating requires either a sustained PAT recovery or a structural unlock that is not yet visible. The biggest risk is that the cess-expiry margin compression is permanent — the street is still repricing this, with sell-side EPS estimates cut -8.8% over 90 days — making the cheap multiple a value trap until a clear earnings inflection quarter arrives.

Hindustan Unilever is one of India's largest FMCG companies, with a ₹5.0L cr market cap and a broad home and personal care business. On P/E, the yardstick for this sector, valuation is fair: trailing 46.6x is within the 40-65x FMCG norm and about 6% above the 43.8x peer median, while forward P/E and EV/EBITDA both rank P80 among peers, and although the stock is near its 52-week low (12.3% of range), the 39.4x forward P/E implies about 18% EPS growth that flat profit does not yet support; I did not rely on the 212% dividend yield, the 3.02 debt/equity or the +21% consensus upside, because they look unreliable (that upside implies a price of about ₹1,864, below the ₹2,022 52-week low). On valuation I used P/E and EV/EBITDA against peers: trailing P/E of 24.8x sits below the 28-40x sector band and at P23 among peers, with forward P/E (19.8x) and P/B (2.8x) both at P8, so the grade is cheap. The biggest risk is that the US generics decline and the semaglutide delay keep hitting earnings before new launches can fill the gap.

The biggest risk is that the earnings recovery stalls as NIM compression and above-normal vehicle and microfinance credit costs hold ROA under 1%.

Grasim is a diversified Aditya Birla holding and operating company spanning cement (through UltraTech), financial services (through Aditya Birla Capital), cellulosic fibres, chemicals, Birla Opus paints and renewables. In Q1FY27, consolidated revenue rose 21.4% YoY to Rs 48,716 cr and PAT rose 38.8% to Rs 3,846 cr, with revenue growth up from +16% in Q1FY26 but below the +25% of Q3FY26, while cement EBITDA per tonne of Rs 1,253 in Q4FY26 was above the healthy Rs 900-1,100 range; the true PAT margin gain is about 6.9% to 7.9%, as the table's jump from 3.5% appears to mix profit definitions. On the EV/EBITDA yardstick, I grade valuation as fair: 13.25x is 25.9% below the 17.9x sector median (P27), but that median is lifted by paint companies, while P/B of 2.12x with ROE of just 6.3% and trailing P/E of 42.42x (P73, versus a 37.3x median) do not look cheap, the stock sits at 87.1% of its 52-week range, and no sum-of-the-parts data was available. The biggest risk is that continued Birla Opus investment, with profitability deferred until Rs 10,000 cr of revenue, and the Rs 17,200 cr Solenergi deal could weigh on returns and leverage, while FY-EPS estimates remain down 4.1% over 90 days despite a 2.5% rise over 30 days and Q2FY27 results are due around the 13 November board meeting.

Using the sector card's P/E-plus-yield yardstick for oil marketers, valuation is fair rather than cheap: the 4.71x trailing P/E and 3.74x EV/EBITDA are below the peer medians of 9.2x and 6.1x, but the P/E appears to reflect older, peak earnings, since our rough trailing-12-month PAT of ₹15,800 cr implies about 7.6x, in line with the 7.19x forward P/E and inside the 6-10x policy-priced range, and the 678% dividend yield is a clear data error so yield could not be assessed. fundamental.thesis: Polycab is India's largest wires and cables maker, with about 30-31% share of the organised market. It is scaling a consumer electricals (FMEG) business and a smaller EPC arm, and has net cash of ₹4,520cr and an 11-day working-capital cycle. Revenue growth sped up from +39% YoY in Q1 FY27 to +53% in Q2 FY27 (₹9,900cr), and PAT rose 43% to ₹990cr. PAT margin edged up to 10.0% from 9.4% in FY26. FMEG grew 124% and posted its first double-digit EBIT margin (10.1%). Much of the headline growth is copper price pass-through, though: copper rose 40-45% in H1, while wire volumes grew only 10.5% and cable volumes about 5%. Underlying demand is healthy but well below the +53% headline. I graded valuation mainly on EV/EBITDA, which suits this capital-intensive business. At 35.0x it sits close to the sector peer median of 34.0x (P53). Trailing P/E is 53.8x (P50) and forward P/E is 38.5x, which points to expected earnings growth. On the sector card's 50-80x range for electricals this is fair, not cheap, and the stock is at 99.8% of its 52-week range. The main risk is that copper-inflated revenue and record margins revert as commodity prices normalise or UltraTech's entry into wires squeezes pricing. That risk is larger because, in a risk-off market, a stock priced for perfection can lose 30-50% of its valuation multiple quickly.

AU Small Finance Bank is a mid-sized retail lender focused on vehicle loans, mortgages and small-business credit, and it is awaiting final approval to become a universal bank. In Q2FY27, revenue grew 25.7% YoY to Rs 3,590 cr (up from +18.7% in Q1) and PAT grew 52.9% to Rs 858 cr (up from +37.0%), with loan growth at 25.1%, but NIM slipped from 5.9% to 5.8%, net NPA rose from 0.76% to 0.81% and provision coverage fell from 85% to 83%, although gross NPA improved from 2.10% to 1.99% and CASA from 29.0% to 29.5%; the 'contracting margin' signal looks like a data artefact because Q1 and Q2 revenue sum to Rs 6,974 cr against Rs 12,374 cr for H1, which suggests mixed revenue definitions. Using P/B with ROE, the right yardstick for a lender, the stock is expensive: P/B of 3.64x (about 3.45x on September net worth) is the highest in its peer set against a 1.5x median, and FY26 ROE of 14.2% (about 16% on annualised Q2 profit) only partly justifies this, even allowing for lower-growth PSU banks in that set; the 27.8x trailing P/E also looks stale (about 23x on our trailing profit estimate), and the 10% dividend yield and consensus upside of 26.3% look unreliable because the market cap and 52-week position imply a price near Rs 970, or about 12% upside to the mean target. The biggest risk is that a premium valuation leaves little room for error if the guided rise in credit costs (about 90 bps for the full year against about 80 bps now) or deposit competition squeezes margins, while final universal bank approval is still pending.

fundamental.thesis: Bank of India is a government-controlled public sector bank (73.4% government ownership) with a ₹9.27 lakh crore deposit base, growing advances about 16% YoY in FY26 against roughly 13.6% deposit growth. The extracted data is incomplete. FY26 PAT grew about 14-15% to roughly ₹10,500 cr, but core net interest income rose only 3% and NIM is a thin 2.52%. Gross NPA improved from 2.26% (Q3FY26) to 1.98% (FY26), and provision coverage rose to 94.45% in H1FY27. Profit growth is therefore coming from lower credit costs and other income, not from lending spreads, and the Q2FY27 results filed on 2026-10-23 have not been extracted yet, so the latest-quarter trend is unconfirmed. On the lender yardstick (price-to-book plus ROE), the stock trades at 0.74x book against a 12-15% ROE, the cheapest in its 15-bank peer set on P/B (P0) and about 50% below the 1.5x median, which grades as cheap. The main risk is margin squeeze: loans are growing faster than deposits, NII growth is flat, and the rate-cut cycle is repricing loan yields down faster than deposit costs, which could stall earnings once the boost from lower provisioning fades.

LIC Housing Finance is a large LIC-backed home lender with a Rs 3.26 lakh crore loan book, about 85% of it individual home loans (March 2026). In Q2 FY27, revenue rose 1.4% YoY to Rs 7,175 cr, recovering from -1.4% in Q1 but still below FY26's +2.6%, while PAT rose 11.4% to Rs 1,509 cr (Q1: +9.9%) and PAT margin held near 21%; core growth is much slower, with NII up 2%, loans up 5%, and NIM down from 2.62% to 2.58%, while Stage 3 loans improved from 2.51% to 2.05%. Using P/B plus ROE, the right yardstick for a lender, the stock looks cheap at 0.75x book with ROE of about 14%, against a Financials peer median of about 2.0x (P3), and its 5.3x trailing P/E is only a cross-check; the 181% dividend yield and +19.1% target upside were ignored because they look like data errors, since the stock's market cap and 52-week position imply a price near Rs 563, or only about 4% below the Rs 588 mean target. The biggest risk is that this is a value trap: profit is growing much faster than NII, which suggests help from lower credit costs rather than core lending, while FY and next-FY EPS estimates have been cut by 2.6% and 3.5% over 90 days.

fundamental.thesis: Sundaram Finance is a premium TVS Group NBFC with ~₹92,887cr consolidated group AUM spanning commercial-vehicle/vehicle financing, home finance (Sundaram Home Finance), asset management (Sundaram AMC), and general insurance (Royal Sundaram), known historically for conservative underwriting and best-in-class asset quality in the CV segment. Q1FY27 consolidated PAT surged +33.9% YoY to ₹636cr — a sharp re-acceleration from FY26's full-year +9.5% PAT growth — with ROA improving sequentially to 3.06% from 2.91%, net NPA declining to 1.35% from 1.71%, and loan growth holding steady at 17% YoY; the operating trajectory is genuinely improving even as AUM growth decelerates mildly (17% → 16% → 15% over three periods), and the group subsidiaries (home finance +37% PAT, AMC +13% PAT) add earnings diversification. Using P/B + ROE as the correct NBFC yardstick (per sector card — P/E explicitly deprioritised for lenders), P/B of 3.51× with estimated ROE ~15% (derived from ROA 3.06% × leverage multiple) rates as fair; trailing P/E of 23.35× is within the NBFC benchmark range (18–28×), but forward P/E ranks at P100 among Credit Services peers (+45.4% premium vs sector median 14.6×), signalling the stock is fully priced for near-term earnings, and the 52-week position at 42.8% of range offers only modest entry comfort in a RISK_OFF tape. The dominant structural risk is the Capital Adequacy Ratio declining from 20.0% to 18.5% over four consecutive periods, compressing balance-sheet expansion headroom and raising the prospect of a dilutive capital raise, while rising crude at $89.72 creates incremental stress on the CV borrower book precisely when macro conditions are already tightening.

Q2FY27 revenue rose 18.5% YoY to Rs 11,601 cr, similar to Q1's reported +18.2%, while PAT rose from Rs 5.91 cr to Rs 100.30 cr, but that +1,597% reflects a very low base, and PAT fell from Rs 118 cr in Q1 as margin slipped from 1.6% to 0.86%; the pre-computed 'accelerating' and 'expanding' signals mix quarterly, half-year and nine-month periods, and the Q1 and H1 revenue figures do not reconcile, so I give them little weight. The right yardstick for a life insurer is P/EV alongside VNB margin and APE growth, none of which were provided, so I grade valuation a low-confidence fair by default: the 682.7x trailing P/E, 20.3x P/B and top-of-peer-group ranks (forward P/E 102.3x vs 46.0x median) lean expensive but are weak measures for this business, and the +55% consensus upside looks wrong because the Rs 1,861 mean target is only about 15% above the roughly Rs 1,620 price implied by the 52-week range. The biggest risk is that the proposed merger of MFSL into Axis Max Life still needs IRDAI and shareholder approvals, while the available data cannot confirm whether the insurer's underlying profitability is improving, and FY estimates have edged down 0.3-0.8% over 90 days.

Q1FY27 revenue grew 19.1% YoY to ₹798 cr, accelerating sharply from the 10.6–10.7% band seen in Q2–Q3FY26; PAT grew faster at 28% YoY to ₹170 cr with EBITDA margin expanding to 35.0% (from a prior-quarter range of 26.6–30.7%), confirming that operating leverage is kicking in as volume scales over a relatively fixed cost base. NATCO Pharma is a mid-cap maker of complex US generics (especially niche oncology products) with a fast-growing India business; FDA compliance looks clean, and it recently launched generic Carboplatin injection in the US. On P/E (the standard pharma yardstick), the trailing 11.2x looks very cheap against the 28–40x sector band and sits at P9 among peers, but that figure is inflated by one-off earnings; on forward P/E of 19.3x (P36) and EV/EBITDA of 9.6x it looks only fair for a business whose profits are shrinking, and the recently allotted rights issue of about 1.7 cr shares dilutes per-share earnings further. The biggest risk is how the ₹2,000 cr raised for M&A gets spent, plus US generic price erosion and the pending US tariff review of generics, before new launches such as Carfilzomib (calendar 2027) can replace the lost windfall.

On valuation, I used P/E and EV/EBITDA together, and the stock looks fair rather than cheap: trailing P/E of 22.6x sits at the bottom of the 22–30x IT range, and EV/EBITDA of 11.4x ranks P16 against the broad market, but ROE is only 7.8%. The low 11.9x forward P/E rests on analyst estimates that were cut 18% over the last 90 days, so it should not be trusted yet. The biggest risk is that semiconductor losses and integrating TAO keep eating into the steady DET profits, and the data has gaps: the yfinance Q2 revenue of ₹1,498 cr conflicts with the filings, Q1FY27 shows two different growth rates, and the reported debt/equity and dividend-yield figures look like data errors.

The primary risk is that PAT margin erosion continues — elevated subcontracting, AI-driven pricing pressure on legacy services, anomalously high D/E of 1.68 for an asset-light IT business, and 90-day EPS revisions of -3.8% all point toward a value trap rather than a mean-reversion opportunity.

Adani Energy Solutions is India's largest private power-transmission company, with about 30% market share, plus the Mumbai distribution business and a fast-growing smart-meter platform, which together form a regulated-asset compounder funded by heavy borrowing. H1 FY27 revenue rose 47.5% YoY to ₹19,787 cr and PAT rose 137% to ₹2,600 cr; backing out Q1 (₹9,711 cr revenue, ₹1,149 cr PAT) gives an implied Q2 of about ₹10,076 cr revenue (about +53% YoY) and ₹1,451 cr PAT (about 14.4% margin), so growth is accelerating and margins are improving. However, part of the revenue jump is low-margin Mumbai distribution pass-through, and earlier-period figures are internally inconsistent (9M FY26 revenue exceeds full-year FY26). On the capital-intensive yardstick the sector card favours, EV/EBITDA of 25.1x is far above what regulated utility annuities typically command, and P/B of 7.2x against ROE of only 9.7% plus a trailing P/E of 81.7x (P88 vs the broad market) make the stock expensive even after allowing for strong growth, rising sell-side estimates (FY EPS +16% over 30 days) and the price sitting near its 52-week high (89.5% of range). The biggest risk is the balance sheet: net debt of about ₹49,156 cr (6.2x FY26 EBITDA), negative free cash flow (H1 FCF of -₹3,185 cr, with ₹21–25k cr of annual capex guided), and Adani-group governance risk leave little room for error if execution slips or interest rates stay high.

Adani Total Gas is a city gas distributor selling CNG to vehicles and piped gas to homes and industry, a regulated volume business that is closer to a utility than to an oil company. rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)
rules.rank: revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth == strong, risk != high, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session

rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); between signal dates the book holds except on a flip, when survivors are rebalanced (no entries or exits)
rules.universe: close > own 200-day SMA, 12-1 momentum known AND the shared fundamental filter (growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes))
rules.exit: rank > 60, close < 200-day SMA, fundamental deterioration (growth -> weak / risk -> high)
rules.entry: new entries wait until the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; holdings are never sold for timing

books.title: Technical pullback in uptrends
books.hypothesis: Technicals the right way round in a mean-reverting tape: buy the dip in a leader and give it time — a 10-session minimum hold and a 20-session cap keep the edge from being traded away in charges.

rules.universe: close > 200-day SMA and 12-1 momentum in the top 20% of names with momentum
rules.entry: 5-session return <= -4% or close < 20-day SMA; ranked by momentum (strongest first)
rules.hold: minimum 10 sessions from the fill (the stop still applies)
rules.exit: after the minimum hold, close >= 20-day SMA or 20 sessions held; -10% from the fill price at any time

books.title: Macro + fundamental, sector rotation
books.hypothesis: Top-down sector timing adds to the bottom-up filter (strong, non-decelerating growers). Judged against b6_neutral — the same construction with every tilt at 1.0 — by more than the random band, plus the sector-call scorecard at one month (>= 60% hit, >= +1 pp per call, model months only); at least 6-8 monthly calls before any judgement, two quarters the floor.

rules.signal: monthly — first session of the calendar month (or the first run after it); one sector_strategist call; none on other days or in a dry run
rules.tilt: per sector in [0.5, 2.0], clamped; sum of |change| per signal capped at 1.0; weights normalised to 1 over sectors with eligible names (neutral = equal share); fallback = the standing tilt (neutral at first)
rules.eligible: the shared fundamental filter: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes); ranked by revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.slots: 30 slots apportioned over the active sectors by largest remainder on w_s x 30 (sum = 30 exactly), with hysteresis: a sector's count changes only when its exact share moves > 0.5 slot from its current allocation; weight w_s / k_s each, capped at 2/30
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); rebalanced on the monthly signal date and on the flip
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions or exited in the last 20 sessions
rules.exit: fundamental deterioration (growth -> weak / risk -> high), or a tilt cut dropping k_s below the names held (lowest-ranked sold first); never on missing data, decelerating growth or timing
rules.rebalance: signal dates and the session the overlay flips; survivors outside +/-25% of target
rules.attribution: monthly Brinson vs the equal-weight universe + sector-call scorecard per signal at +5 / +21 / +63 sessions (the 1m row judges; leaderboard key book6_attribution)
rules.judge: Book 6 minus b6_neutral (the same construction, every tilt 1.0, zero LLM) must exceed the random band; scorecard at 1m >= 60% hit and >= +1 pp per call, over- and under-weights each above their own null (~45% / ~55%), model months only; at least 6-8 monthly calls before any judgement (two quarters is the floor)

books.title: Fundamental grades → rules, old filter (a)
books.hypothesis: The pre-c1 Book 3 — moderate growers and the conviction leg, no acceleration leg — run live beside Book 3 to settle c1 vs (a) out of sample (the first 98-session replay had (a) ahead).

rules.eligible: growth in {strong, moderate}, risk != high, data_quality != poor, conviction >= 0.5 (fundamental_filter_v1, the original rule (a))
rules.rank: growth grade (strong first), then conviction, then symbol
rules.entry: next open; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions (no results-timing leg); slots freed by sells are refilled the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth in {strong, moderate}, risk != high, conviction >= 0.5 (rule (a) without the data-quality leg), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (rule (a) no longer met); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
rules.review_gate: growth in {strong, moderate}, risk != high, conviction >= 0.5

books.title: Growth screen (ranked by PAT growth)
books.hypothesis: Avoid what the grades call losers (high risk, weak growth, poor data, decelerating), then buy the highest reported revenue growth — the one fundamental the winners forensic found on the winners' side — with Book 3's construction.

rules.eligible: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)
rules.rank: PAT growth YoY from the filings, highest first (missing last), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass the same filter, else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, or the 120-session review failing (the same filter); no sentiment exit

books.kill_rule: more than 10 points behind the equal-weight null on a rolling 60-date basis, twice in a row
books.promote_rule: best book at 90 dates, if ahead of both benchmarks

brinson.method: Brinson-Fachler vs the equal-weight universe, start-of-month holdings held through the month; Cash is a sector with zero return and zero benchmark weight
